text:
Jason Zucker's season has been a slog. He has one point in eight games, a power-play goal against Philadelphia, and he's been held off the scoresheet in seven straight since. His ice time has dropped to about 12 minutes a night, three and a quarter below where it was last season.

The frustrating part is that he's still getting to good ice. His own chance rate is 1.84 expected goals per 60, higher than his strong 2025-26, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him getting to the slot more than most forwards. One goal on 3.0 expected is bad finishing, and Buffalo has scored 5.6 fewer goals than expected with him on the ice.

The worry is everything else. The Sabres have 43.3% of the five-on-five expected goals in his minutes, 8.4 points worse than the team does without him, and his skating numbers sit near the bottom of the league. At 34, coming off a 24-goal season, he can still finish. Our range has him around 17 goals from here, if Lindy Ruff keeps giving him the minutes.
headline: Jason Zucker is getting chances and nothing else
